$comment: Cross-SDK disagreements that are known, understood, and being worked. Every entry needs a reason and a hard expiry. NEW drift fails the run; an expired entry fails the run; and a recorded entry whose SDKs now AGREE also fails, because a note describing a state that no longer exists is the same rot as a stale finding. Baseline taken 2026-08-13 from the first three-SDK run (python, go, typescript). Nothing here is acceptable — it is the work list. 2026-08-13 later the same day: nine entries removed after the TypeScript int8 coercion, pathIn decode and datalog arity fixes landed — the runner refuses to keep an entry whose SDKs now agree.

drift.reason: S22 decided the contract — get_path returns the VALUE — and landed it in Python only. Go (document.go PathIn) and TypeScript (pathIn) still return the engine's raw JSON text, so a string arrives as '"ada"'. Port the decode.

Three different answers to the same question. Python synthesizes raw point retrieval from 60 bucketed TS_RANGE_AVG calls. Go's TimeSeries.Query refuses outright with 'raw point retrieval is not supported by the engine' — which is false, since Python does it on the same primitives. TypeScript has no raw point read at all. Decide once whether the SDK owns this synthesis, then make all three agree.

Go and TypeScript both return CDC events as a raw JSON STRING rather than a list; Go has no CDCEvent type at all. Latent false green risk: a non-empty string is truthy, so a nonEmpty assertion would pass on an empty result.

Two engine defects behind one case (see the spec's xfail note), plus TypeScript's VectorModel having no count(), so it cannot run the case at all. Also worth fixing while here: TypeScript's search score is inverted — score = dist > 0 ? 1/dist : 0, so an exact match scores 0 and a worse match scores 1. And Go's Vector.Search panics on nil-metadata inserts, which is the documented default call.

The statement-Describe defect only reaches clients that describe before binding. asyncpg does and fails; node-postgres binds first and passes, so TypeScript xpasses. Not drift between SDKs so much as drift between driver strategies — but it stays recorded until the engine describes the column correctly, because until then the two clients genuinely disagree about what the database returns.
Same statement-Describe defect. Additionally Go decodes uuid to a 16-byte array rather than a string, which is container drift the expectation vocabulary cannot currently express.

Same statement-Describe defect; Go and TypeScript both return 1 correctly, asyncpg gets raw big-endian bytes. Note separately that go/nucleus/sql.go forces pgx.QueryExecModeSimpleProtocol on every Query/QueryOne/Exec, so Go interpolates parameters into the statement text and cannot exercise the binary parameter path at all — its pass here is not evidence the path works.
